subject: Technical demo request from Docs Quickstart — BuildFlux
messages:
From: BuildFlux Developer Intake Form <no-reply@docs.redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: New inbound demo request — BuildFlux (Developer intent)

A new developer-intent demo request was submitted from the Quickstart CTA. Details below.

Name: Samantha Lee
Role: Senior Backend Engineer
Company: BuildFlux
Email: samantha@buildflux.com
Company size: 45 engineers
Primary use case: inference routing for feature flags + multi-model fallback
Notes: "We tried the quickstart and hit performance variability when scaling to bursts. Interested in how Redwood handles KV caching and routing to cheaper model variants for non-critical requests."
Preferred contact window: Weekday mornings (PST)

--
This email was generated by the Docs Quickstart form. If you are not the right owner, please reassign in HubSpot.
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@buildflux.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 10:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: New inbound demo request — BuildFlux (Developer intent)

Hi Samantha — thanks for signing up and for the clear notes. I’m Priyom on the developer success / SDR team. Ben (cc) is our technical AE and will join the call for the architecture bits.

Quick plan: 30-minute technical walkthrough to cover your quickstart notes (KV cache behavior, routing and quantization profiles) + a short Q&A. Would any of these work for you?
- Tue Mar 7, 9:30–10:00am PST
- Tue Mar 7, 11:00–11:30am PST
- Wed Mar 8, 8:30–9:00am PST

If those don’t match, feel free to pick a slot on my calendar: https://calendly.com/priyom-das/30min

I’ve attached a one-page scope that maps what we typically cover for developer-intent demos — helps us keep the call focused.

Agenda (proposed):
1) Short intro + short reproducible steps from your quickstart attempt
2) How our runtime handles prefix/KV caching and routing policies
3) Latency/cost trade-offs and recommended config for bursty workloads
4) Next steps (POC/dev access or Dedicated evaluation)

Thanks — let me know which slot you prefer and any attendees from your side.

Best,
Priyom Das
Developer Success | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Attachment: quickstart-scope.pdf (1 page)
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@buildflux.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 11:12:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: New inbound demo request — BuildFlux (Developer intent)

Thanks Priyom — appreciate the quick reply. 11:00–11:30am PST on Tue Mar 7 works for me. I’ll invite our infra lead (Tom Nguyen) as well — he’s mainly worried about cold-starts during bursts.

One quick question: we’re running a couple models in mixed precision; is it helpful to share a short profile (token lengths, avg tokens per request) ahead of time?

Subject: Re: New inbound demo request — BuildFlux (Developer intent)

Perfect — confirmed for Tue Mar 7, 11:00–11:30am PST. I’ve sent a calendar invite with a Google Meet link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-pqrs-tuv

Ben and I will cover the runtime internals and we’ll leave ~10 minutes for your infra questions. If you can drop a short profile (avg tokens, peak RPS, and whether you use KV caching now) into this thread or upload to the HubSpot contact we’ll tailor the demo to your numbers.

Quick pre-call checklist:
- Share a small sample of request patterns (anonymized) if possible
- Confirm attendees (name + role) — Tom, anyone else from infra?
- Any hard constraints (SLA, region, on-prem requirement) we should know about

Looking forward — I’ve cc’d Ben so he can prep a short slide on quantization and fallback variants.

See you Tuesday,
Priyom Das
Developer Success | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142
